name: IEC hysteresis (bi-threshold) qualifier
summary: Small hysteresis loop mark showing a Schmitt-trigger function or a bi-threshold input.
description: The hysteresis mark, a small loop drawn with two offset steps, appears either as a general qualifier for a Schmitt-trigger element or next to a single input to show that input has two thresholds. TI's public overview lists both uses.

When the mark is next to one input only, the other inputs of the element have normal single thresholds. That matters on devices such as gates with one Schmitt input used to accept a slow external signal.
The mark does not quantify hysteresis. Threshold and hysteresis values must be read from device data and compared with the signal source.
readingNotes: Check whether the mark applies to the whole element or one input.
Compare thresholds with the signal source levels.
drawingChecklist: Draw the mark clearly, not as a waveform sketch.
Place it at the input it applies to where only some inputs have hysteresis.
distinction: A drawn square-wave inside a G element indicates an astable, not hysteresis.
